clue.text: Sins with time on hands, son admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the letter for son is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in letter headings
hands as a verb means passes, as in hands over
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A confession of wrongdoing committed in idle moments, with a son allowed in on the secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' is a verb here, not body parts; 'admitted' lets the son letter in just before the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespasses is the old Lord's Prayer word for sins or wrongdoings, as in 'forgive us our trespasses'.

clue.text: Obsession with self-image on a shot

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on their own image, chasing one more photo shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-image' is split across definition and wordplay: 'self' ends the definition, and 'shot' (meaning ruined) shuffles the next two words, with A added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an extreme, obsessive preoccupation with oneself and one's own importance.

clue.text: Filling canine with hole at the front, cutting into infected area

indicators.note: cutting into means slicing inside, so the altered canine word goes within the infected-area word

parts.note: a sty is an infected swelling on the eyelid

indicators.note: at the front tells us the hole letter is shifted to the start of the canine word

parts.note: a dog is a canine
O is a hole, from its round shape

explanation.surface: A dentist filling a canine tooth that has a cavity at the front, working around an infected patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' and 'canine' suggest dentistry, but filling is the adjective for heavy food. 'at the front' shifts the hole letter to the start, then 'cutting into' places the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy food is heavy and filling, like suet pudding.

clue.text: Roll cigars at the back with habit

indicators.note: at the back points to the final letter of the word cigars

parts.note: a way is a habit or custom, as in 'set in one's ways'

explanation.surface: Rolling cigars out back, as is one's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway is to roll or rock from side to side, as a ship does.

clue.text: See 8
Short underwear is more flashy

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the underwear word loses its final letter

parts.note: a brassiere is an item of women's underwear

explanation.surface: Skimpier underwear makes for a showier look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the final E of BRASSIERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy means showy or loud, so brassier is the comparative: more showy.

clue.text: Tycoon with no money from a common male ancestor

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the money letter is dropped from the tycoon word

parts.note: a magnate is a tycoon, a wealthy business leader

explanation.surface: A tycoon left penniless, cast off from the family line.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnate describes relatives descended through the male line from the same forefather.

clue.text: Tories' lying has extraordinary scale: that's what they do

indicators.note: extraordinary in the sense of out of the ordinary order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that Conservative politicians lie on a remarkable scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' looks like the size of the lying; it is the verb, as in scaling teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental hygienists remove tartar from teeth, a job called scaling.

clue.text: Like a shot that's one foot off

parts.note: the right is one of a person's two feet
away means off, as in 'off on holiday'

explanation.surface: A remark on a football shot that went a foot wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for immediately, without delay.

clue.text: I picked up that man

explanation.surface: Someone saying they gave a man a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure 'roger' confirms a message has been received, and Roger is also a given name for a man.

clue.text: Rallies around a year later

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the rallies word is read backwards

parts.note: demos are protest rallies

explanation.surface: Protest rallies come round again a year later.
explanation.definitionFit: Someday means at some unspecified future time, so eventually or later on.

clue.text: Plant not out by hedge

parts.note: a cricket batsman who is not out is still in
to hedge is to stall or avoid committing

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: keep a plant indoors next to the hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to set it in place, which is to install it.

clue.text: Number getting into some trouble

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the number abbreviation goes inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A figure who finds themselves in a bit of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to bother or irritate them, as annoy does.

clue.text: Europe perhaps able to control movement

definitions.meaning: Europe is an example of a ...

explanation.surface: Europe pictured as a body with a tight grip on migration.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one of the world's large landmasses; separately, a continent person can control their bladder and bowel movements.

clue.text: Brilliant nurses opposed to support from just one side

indicators.note: nurses means holds close, so the brilliant word wraps around the opposed word

parts.note: clever means brilliant or bright
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Talented nurses who are against a policy back it from one side only.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a beam fixed at only one end, bearing a load such as a balcony.

clue.text: All settees, when rearranged, fit together

indicators.note: rearranged means put in a different order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Moving all the sofas around until they fit the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapes tessellate when they cover a surface without gaps or overlaps, like tiles.

clue.text: Standard partners getting off with sadists

indicators.note: getting off in the sense of becoming aroused, a lively change that rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: A racy picture of couples taking their pleasure with sadists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective; it is a flag, the US Stars and Stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the Stars and Stripes is the flag of the United States.

clue.text: Bank, embroiled with lies, could go under

indicators.note: embroiled means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bank caught up in deceit might collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinkable is capable of going under water, of foundering.

clue.text: Get sex partner on top

parts.note: in British slang to pull is to pick up a romantic or sexual partner
over means on top of, as on means over

explanation.surface: Crude advice about getting a lover to climb on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is the garment, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a jumper, a knitted top pulled on over the head.

clue.text: School uniform matches period in history

parts.note: even means uniform or regular
ties are drawn matches

explanation.surface: A school blazer and tie that look like a period costume.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seventies were the decade 1970 to 1979, a period of history.

clue.text: Mentioned bill? Not during date

indicators.note: not means without, so the during word is removed from the bill word

parts.note: an invoice is a bill
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: Someone raised the matter of the bill, but not on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice something is to express or mention it, so voiced means mentioned.

clue.text: Deliver new stock of local vegetables

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, as the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A greengrocer bringing in a fresh supply of local produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new stock' sounds like goods for a shop; it means a newborn animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow that calves gives birth, delivering a new addition to the livestock.

clue.text: Cover one in crib

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the one word goes within the crib word

parts.note: to crib is to copy
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A cover fitted over a baby's crib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' looks like a cot; it is copying.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is a cloth cover hung above a bed or throne.

clue.text: Secret Service after prince over Virginia

indicators.note: after places the service word behind the prince letter
over means covering, so the service word lies around the state abbreviation

parts.note: a rite is a religious service
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: The Secret Service following a prince across Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret Service' reads as one phrase; it splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Private means kept secret, confidential.

clue.text: Upright position

explanation.definitionFit: A post is an upright stake of wood or metal, and also a job or appointment.

clue.text: Container with hamper gives protection for food

parts.note: a tin is a container
to foil is to hamper or thwart

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper and a box keep food protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil, or kitchen foil, is wrapped around food to keep it fresh.

clue.text: Tough husband wearing drag

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the drag word goes around the husband letter

parts.note: to tug is to drag or pull

explanation.surface: A rough-looking husband dressed in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' suggests women's clothing; it is a pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough as a noun is a rough, violent person, which is a thug.

clue.text: Knock off bails, ultimately getting duck

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of bails is taken

parts.note: a teal is a kind of duck

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: knocking the bails off and out for a duck, a score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Knock off is slang for steal, as in knocked-off goods.

clue.text: Group of players mostly penning quiet pieces for instruments

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the shortened group wraps around the following pieces
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Equity is the UK actors' union, a body of players
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A band holding quiet pieces for its instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity, the British actors' union, is the 'group of players', not a band; 'mostly' trims its last letter and 'penning' encloses the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is the general term for tools and apparatus, which are instruments.
